title: 2013 AMC 10B Problem 20
statement: The number \(2013\) is expressed in the form \[2013 = \frac {a_1!a_2!\cdots a_m!}{b_1!b_2!\cdots b_n!},\] where \[a_1 \ge a_2 \ge \cdots \ge a_m\] and \[b_1 \ge b_2 \ge \cdots \ge b_n\] are positive integers and \(a_1 + b_1\) is as small as possible. What is \(|a_1 - b_1|?\)

solutions.text:
The prime factorization is \(2013=3\cdot11\cdot61\), so the numerator must contain a factor of \(61\). Hence \(a_1\ge61\).

But \(61!\) also contains the prime factor \(59\), which is not in \(2013\), so the denominator must contain a factor of \(59\). Hence \(b_1\ge59\).

The lower bound \(a_1+b_1\ge120\) is attainable because \(2013=\frac{61!\,11!\,3!}{59!\,10!\,5!}\).

Thus \(|a_1-b_1|=61-59=2\), and the correct answer is B .
hints: The numerator must include a factor of \(61\)
Any unwanted prime below \(61\), especially \(59\), must be canceled from the denominator
